title: Hopper FP8: telemetry-driven per-device autotuner and stability gates
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Safely enable FP8 (E4M3/E5M2) profiles across Hopper devices by building a per-device autotuner that uses live telemetry and statistical stability gates to decide profile activation and automated rollback. This ticket builds the autotuner service, defines stability signatures, integrates golden-eval hooks, and codifies a conservative rollout path (shadow -> canary -> progressive).

Why: Existing bulk calibration pipelines assume homogeneous device behavior. In practice, Hopper silicon and driver variations produce per-device quantization sensitivity. A telemetry-driven autotuner reduces false positives, limits user-facing regressions, and lets us unlock FP8 cost benefits with bounded risk.

Scope:
- Per-device profiling harness to collect activation fingerprints (per-layer scale histograms, outlier counts, cross-batch variance) during shadow runs.
- Autotuner algorithm: selects E4M3 vs E5M2 per-device using stability score + runtime heuristics (latency/throughput impact), with hysteresis and cooldown.
- Stability gates: statistical tests (KS-test on activation distributions, variance thresholds, median-perplexity delta) that must pass before activation.
- Golden-eval integration: run canonical prompt set on canary fleet and compare against golden outputs (both accuracy and structural diffs).
- Rollout orchestration: shadow deployments -> 5% canary -> 25% progressive -> full, with automatic rollback triggers.
- Observability and alerts: dashboards, SLI/SLOs, and automated incident pages for regression events.

Non-goals: building per-workload model retraining or changing model weights. This ticket focuses on inference-time calibration and activation mechanics only.
tasks: Implement per-device profiling agent (collection + upload schema)
Prototype autotuner service and optimizer that recommends E4M3/E5M2 per device
Define and implement statistical stability gate checks (KS-test, variance thresholds, delta-ppl)
Wire golden-eval harness and reporting to CI/CD for canary validation
Integrate rollout controller with our existing deployment engine (shadow/canary/progress)
Add dashboards and alert rules for accuracy regressions and latency regressions
Write runbook for on-call with rollback/playbook steps
acceptance_criteria:
1) Autotuner produces a stable per-device profile recommendation endpoint and logs human-readable decision reasons.
2) Shadow runs on 100 devices produce telemetry that meets collection SLA (>=95% sample coverage).
3) Canary run against 5% of traffic shows no accuracy regression >0.5% absolute on golden-eval set and no latency P95 increase >10ms.
4) Automated rollout and rollback triggers fire correctly in simulated fail cases.
5) Runbook documented and reviewed by SRE, ML infra, and Product.
risks: Device-level drift causing intermittent accuracy regressions not caught by small canaries
Telemetry sampling bias (hot/rare routes underrepresented in shadow runs)
False positive stability gate failures blocking valid activations
In-flight KV cache incompatibilities when switching quant profiles causing increased latency
Operational complexity: more frequent per-device decisions may complicate debugging
